title: Tubulin-cryptophycin Ring Polymers Studied by Single-molecule Methods: Deep-etch Electron Microscopy and Mass Photometry
content:
Abstract
Tubulin is the target of numerous small molecules that alter microtubule (MT) polymerization, including the cryptophycins. Cryptophycin 1 (Cp1) and Cp52 both inhibit MT polymerization and promote formation of tightly curved ring polymers composed of a single protofilament of tubulin dimers. These rings are studied here using two methods that provide information about individual molecules: deep-etch rotary platinum replica electron microscopy and mass photometry. Both methods reveal the presence of eight- and nine-dimer rings and rare larger rings, as well as smaller tubulin oligomers and tubulin monomers and dimers.
